subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI scroll-jump fix be owned as renderer/viewport anchoring, as an upstream pi-tui patch, or as a new user-facing TUI auto-scroll/preserve mode?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the permanent behavior changes terminal UX and may cross the third-party renderer boundary or add a new user-facing mode.

options.title: Repair anchoring first
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping the terminal viewport, then follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add an explicit TUI scroll mode
options.body: Expose a terminal user control for follow/preserve behavior, accepting the extra option, docs, tests, and upgrade-proof burden.

options.title: Wait for live proof or upstream
options.body: Keep the tracker open until a current-main PTY capture or upstream pi-tui fix proves the exact repair path.

recommendation.title: Repair anchoring first
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping the terminal viewport, then follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest recent owner signal for the current TUI ChatLog and event-handler state path that would need to encode the decision.
